 Public Works boosts govt building readiness for rainy season
 November 13, 2026 / 7:09 PM 
 Share 
 Sharjah24: Sharjah’s Department of Public Works affirmed readiness for the rainy season by improving government buildings whose operational maintenance it oversees. The department is carrying out inspections and preventive maintenance and strengthening its monitoring and field response capabilities to protect building users and keep services running in different weather conditions.
 Inspections and preventive maintenance 
 The department is checking safety and security measures across 430 buildings containing 65,000 assets, which are managed by specialist teams comprising 65 technicians and inspectors. The checks include inspecting the roofs of all government buildings under its supervision to prevent leaks during rainfall and confirm that the buildings are ready for the season.
 The plan also includes clearing stormwater drainage openings across all its projects and carrying out preventive maintenance, including waterproofing, so teams can act immediately if water accumulates. Based on meteorological forecasts, the department deploys teams across all project sites several hours before strong winds are expected. It has also mobilised specialist field teams and provided the equipment and machinery needed to deal with standing water and other weather-related incidents, helping teams respond faster and protect building users.
 Round-the-clock monitoring and early alerts 
 The department uses its smart ‘Baad’ platform to monitor government projects and facilities remotely around the clock. The platform uses advanced sensors and AI-powered data analysis to detect faults before a maintenance request is needed, allowing teams to intervene quickly and support the long-term upkeep of government facilities. It also helps identify potential risks, issue alerts and guide preventive action to protect property.
 Emergency response and construction site safety 
 To strengthen operational readiness, the department is helping teams make faster decisions and is coordinating with the relevant authorities to dispatch emergency and maintenance crews to affected sites.
 During periods of rain and strong winds, the department sends text messages urging contractors and engineering consultancies to take precautions at worksites. It asks them to secure movable equipment such as tower cranes and external platforms, as well as construction materials that could be blown away, including galvanised steel sheets, wooden boards and similar items, to prevent damage.
 Protecting lives, property and essential services 
 Engineer Hadef Al Khader, Director of the department’s Maintenance Directorate, said protecting lives and property and keeping essential services running are central to its plans. He said preparations for the rainy season begin early, with assessments of building readiness, identification of priority sites and efforts to strengthen field teams’ ability to respond effectively to different weather conditions.
 According to Al Khader, the department is proactively reinforcing infrastructure to better weather shifting climatic trends, placing a strong emphasis on rapid response capabilities. He noted that officials are currently rolling out an integrated framework combining routine preventive maintenance, around-the-clock monitoring, and seamless field coordination to safeguard occupants and ensure uninterrupted public services.
 He added that investment in infrastructure improves operational efficiency, strengthens resilience and helps facilities adapt to different climatic conditions. These improvements help meet future development needs and maintain the quality of services provided to the community.
